newsitem.title: FRANCE: French retailers to pay special meat tax - papers.
newsitem.headline: French retailers to pay special meat tax - papers.

text.p: France's National Assembly has approved a meat tax on supermarkets next year to cover the 600 to 700 million franc cost of disposing of animal carcasses and abattoir waste, French newspapers said on Saturday.

A levy of up to one percent of meat purchases excluding value added tax would be imposed next year on supermarkets and other food retailers with more than two million francs of annual turnover, the Figaro and Liberation newspapers reported.
They said Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur was keen not to put the burden of the carcass clean-up costs on meat producers devastated by the mad cow crisis.
Since a ban was introduced in June on the production of meal from bones and abattoir waste, meal producers have no incentive to collect carcasses, which are left to rot in the countryside.
